title: Channels and producer-consumer pipelines
description: Build async pipelines with System.Threading.Channels for efficient producer-consumer data flow.

data.text: `System.Threading.Channels` provides a modern, high-performance way to pass data between producers and consumers asynchronously. Unlike `BlockingCollection`, channels are designed for `async`/`await` and support backpressure out of the box.

A `Channel<T>` has two ends: a writer and a reader. Producers call `WriteAsync` to push items; consumers call `ReadAsync` to pull them. The channel buffers items up to a capacity you choose. When the buffer is full, `WriteAsync` waits until space opens. This natural backpressure prevents producers from overwhelming consumers.

data.title: Creating and using a channel

data.text: Channels shine when you chain multiple stages. For example, a pipeline that reads files, parses JSON, and writes results to a database can run stages concurrently. Each stage runs in its own task, reading from the previous channel and writing to the next.

data.title: Three-stage pipeline
Choose bounded channels for backpressure
data.text: Unbounded channels (`Channel.CreateUnbounded`) can grow without limit if the consumer falls behind. Bounded channels slow the producer automatically, preventing out-of-memory crashes.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Channels pass data between async producers and consumers.
Pipelines chain stages with multiple channels.
Complete each writer when no more items are coming.
